According to Counterpoint Research, even as overall market shipments declined, Apple still accounted for nearly half of global smartphone revenue in the second quarter. Details below.

Apple achieved its highest-ever revenue share in the second quarter

A new report from Counterpoint Research (cited via MacMagazine) pointed out that Apple recorded a 49% share of global smartphone revenue last quarter, a historic high, representing a year-on-year increase of 22% and marking the company's highest second-quarter revenue share on record.

Counterpoint noted that overall smartphone revenue for the quarter grew 7% year-on-year, with Apple being the fastest-growing among the top five brands. Its average selling price rose from US$879 a year ago to US$946.

Apple also recorded its highest-ever second-quarter shipment share, climbing from 17% a year ago to 21%; however, the company still ranked second, trailing behind Samsung, which held a 23% share of global shipments. Shipment shares for the remaining top five brands all declined, with Xiaomi seeing the largest drop, falling from 14% to 11%, and shipments plunging 26% year-on-year.

Counterpoint pointed out that, affected by an industry-wide memory shortage, several smartphone manufacturers were forced to raise prices due to rising component costs and tight supply. At the same time, Apple maintained relatively stable iPhone pricing, although Counterpoint expects this to change in the coming quarters.

Original report:

Counterpoint's report was published after Apple's fiscal third-quarter 2026 earnings call, during which the company warned that supply constraints would significantly intensify in the September quarter, primarily affecting iPhone, iPad and Mac.
